### Summary

On Windows, Chrome-extension-backed Browser Use returned normally from a single `locator.click()` on an X Like button, and later from a single `locator.press('Enter')` on a different X Like button. Separate exact-target reads continued to show the unliked state. The keyboard incident occurred immediately after a reply was successfully submitted with Control+Return and separately verified at its public URL.

This is an observed activation/state mismatch. The original input event, application request and server response were not captured, so I cannot distinguish input non-delivery, event interception or X-side nonacceptance from the saved evidence.

### Environment and version scope

- Windows 11, dedicated Chrome profile through the Codex browser extension.
- Current installed MSIX identity, read on 2026-10-11 JST: OpenAI.Codex `26.1007.2314.0`. This is package metadata, not a freshly read About-dialog display version.
- Current inspected `@oai/browser-desktop/scripts/browser-service.mjs` SHA256: `8c83e93bdca10cdffa9f7af80db7775ddf1d993186dbf4b8b3d32d11e9bd9666`.
- The exact bundle hash and execution-policy mode used by each original incident have not been established. Source findings below apply to the currently installed file.
- No vendor/runtime changes, forced clicks, direct-CDP operations, action retries or additional browser diagnostics were performed for this investigation.

### Observed sequence, 2026-10-10 UTC

| Case | Actual operation and saved result | Separate evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A | One documented locator click returned normally. | Exact target remained unliked on separate read and a later diagnostic approximately49 seconds later. An adjacent like had succeeded in the same browser session. |
| B | Reply Control+Return issued09:24:21.181, returned09:24:21.505. | Independent reply read at09:24:26.904–27.083 verified author, full text, parent and public URL. |
| B | First and only like Enter issued09:25:13.849, returned09:25:14.061. | Exact-target read at09:25:23.097–23.314 remained unliked; later diagnostic at09:26:13.165–13.371 also remained unliked. |

For Case B the post-action diagnostic found one exact article and one Like button, an enabled control, the focused element as that BUTTON, and its center hit-test reaching the button. The current owner page was readable, and captured visible-warning and console-error lists were empty. These post-action checks do not prove what input events the button received at the original dispatch time or rule out an unobserved server response.

The two cases use different targets and input routes. I am not claiming a shared causal root or general X outage. No repeated input was sent to reconcile either uncertain action.

### Current source and isolated checks

I evaluated unchanged excerpts from the installed locator-press handler, keyboard dispatcher, key table and clipboard-shortcut routing in Node VM fixtures. CDP acknowledgements, focus and application acceptance were stubs; no browser or X request was involved. All7 assertions passed:

- Enter and Return both resolve to native Enter, codeEnter, Windows VK13; keyDown with carriage-return text, then keyUp.
- Enter and Control+Return do not enter the virtual-clipboard shortcut route.
- Control+Return releases Control on ordinary completion.
- keyDown and keyUp acknowledgement rejections propagate rather than returning success.
- An unknown key is rejected before input.
- With successful simulated acknowledgements, the same handler result is possible whether simulated application state changes or remains unchanged.

Earlier unchanged-source native-pointer fixtures similarly showed dispatch acknowledgement cannot distinguish simulated application acceptance. Locator click has policy-dependent native and document-scoped branches, and the original incident's selected branch is missing.

These tests narrow current-source mapping/error-handling hypotheses. They do not reproduce the original application failure or establish a fix.

Could the browser runtime expose supported, correlated diagnostics for:

1. The selected execution-policy route and exact runtime bundle/version for the command.
2. Focus/target context, actual input dispatch and acknowledgement timestamps, and whether the intended document received the activation event.
3. A way to distinguish a successful transport acknowledgement from application activation without replaying a state-changing command.

A minimal non-sensitive enabled BUTTON fixture with capture listeners for keydown/keyup/click and a visible activation counter would help compare command acknowledgement with document delivery. It would still need correlation with the original application trace before attributing this incident to browser dispatch rather than X.

### Related reports

- #37855 concerns a Windows popup click with an explicit Runtime.evaluate timeout. These calls returned normally, so this is not established as that timeout.
- #48735 reports silent pointer activation problems in macOS IAB with working keyboard activation. These incidents are Windows Chrome extension-backed, including a keyboard-state mismatch.

items.body:
## Summary

I am integrating the new **open-source Sign in with ChatGPT token-sharing flow** with Codex app-server. A freshly issued app-owned OAuth access token successfully completes a text Responses turn, but `thread/realtime/start` with WebRTC and v3 fails **before an SDP answer or realtime-start event**:

```text
unexpected status 401 Unauthorized: Unauthorized
url: https://api.openai.com/v1/live
auth error: 401
auth error code: no_matching_rule
```

Is Codex Live intended to work with these new OSS SIWC tokens? If so, is an additional token exchange, scope, provider setting, or account header required? If unsupported, please document the boundary between Responses, public Realtime, and Codex Live.

This is the `dynamic_agent_client` / issued-client-ID flow documented at:
- https://developers.openai.com/siwc/token-sharing-open-source/sign-in
- https://developers.openai.com/siwc/token-sharing-open-source/codex-app-server

It is **not** an access token extracted from Codex's managed login, a PAT, or an API key.

## Environment

- Reproduced on October 11, 2026 (JST).
- Windows 11 Pro; desktop host Electron 43.1.1.
- Windows Codex: `0.162.0-alpha.17.2`.
- Ubuntu / WSL Codex: `0.157.0`.
- Also observed previously with Windows Codex `0.146.0-alpha.3.1`.
- A separate managed-Codex login on this machine passes the voice baseline below. Account identity equivalence between the two login routes was not independently verified, so this is not a claim of an account-matched regression.

## Verified behavior

| Test | Result |
| --- | --- |
| New SIWC OAuth: signature, issuer, audience, expiry, nonce and granted plan-use scope | Validated |
| New SIWC: public model catalog | Succeeds |
| New SIWC: app-server text inference on `gpt-6-luna` | `SIWC_CHAT_OK`; `turn/completed` status `completed` |
| New SIWC: native Live v3 / Windows 0.162 | HTTP 401 `no_matching_rule` |
| New SIWC: native Live v3 / WSL 0.157 | HTTP 401 `no_matching_rule` |
| Existing managed Codex login / Windows 0.162 | WebRTC connected; assistant transcript “こんにちは!”; 234 audio packets and 58,897 non-silent samples |

The failing new-SIWC sessions emit `thread/realtime/error`, with no `thread/realtime/sdp` or `thread/realtime/started`. No voice audio is received.

## Reproduction

1. Register and authorize the app using the documented OSS flow: initial `client_id=dynamic_agent_client`, `agent_name_hint=CharaDock`, stable `ext_agent_host_id`, PKCE, state and nonce. Use the issued client ID for the code exchange.
2. Request resource `https://api.openai.com/v1` and scopes:
   `openid profile email offline_access resource.invoke chatgpt.tokens.use.direct`.
3. Pass the returned access token in the app-server child environment as `CHARADOCK_CHATGPT_ACCESS_TOKEN`. Each SIWC probe uses a separate empty `CODEX_HOME`, without a managed login or API key.
4. Start app-server with provider overrides **after** the subcommand:

```sh
codex app-server --stdio --enable realtime_conversation \
  -c 'model_provider="openai_chatgpt_plan"' \
  -c 'model_providers.openai_chatgpt_plan.name="ChatGPT plan"' \
  -c 'model_providers.openai_chatgpt_plan.base_url="https://api.openai.com/v1"' \
  -c 'model_providers.openai_chatgpt_plan.env_key="CHARADOCK_CHATGPT_ACCESS_TOKEN"' \
  -c 'model_providers.openai_chatgpt_plan.wire_api="responses"' \
  -c 'model_providers.openai_chatgpt_plan.requires_openai_auth=false' \
  -c 'model_providers.openai_chatgpt_plan.supports_websockets=false'
```

5. Initialize with `clientInfo.name: "CharaDock"` matching the registration name and `capabilities.experimentalApi: true`; send `initialized`.
6. First verify a completed text turn. Create a fresh empty thread for the voice test.
7. Submit a real browser-generated audio SDP offer using:

```json
{
  "method": "thread/realtime/start",
  "params": {
    "threadId": "<fresh-thread-id>",
    "model": "gpt-live-1-codex",
    "version": "v3",
    "outputModality": "audio",
    "transport": { "type": "webrtc", "sdp": "<valid-audio-SDP-offer>" },
    "includeStartupContext": false,
    "clientManagedHandoffs": false,
    "codexResponseHandoffMode": "bemTags",
    "flushTranscriptTailOnSessionEnd": true
  }
}
```

## Settings checked

- Explicit top-level `model: "gpt-live-1-codex"` and `version: "v3"`, per #40140.
- Fresh OAuth grants and matching app originator. Local capture verified `originator: CharaDock`, `openai-alpha: quicksilver=v2`, the requested model, and the configured environment bearer. The inherited `CODEX_INTERNAL_ORIGINATOR_OVERRIDE` was explicitly set to `CharaDock`.
- Setting `experimental_realtime_webrtc_call_base_url="https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex"` changes the request to `/realtime/calls?intent=quicksilver&architecture=avas`, but still returns 401 `no_matching_rule` using the new SIWC token. It does not select managed-Codex authentication.
- Explicit `gpt-live-1` instead of `gpt-live-1-codex`: same 401.
- Adding `intent=quicksilver&architecture=avas` on the public Live route: same 401.

## Separate public-Realtime observations

These do **not** establish that public Realtime voice is supported by SIWC:

- `POST /v1/realtime/client_secrets` with the new SIWC OAuth bearer and `session: {type:"realtime", model:"gpt-realtime"}` returns HTTP 200 and a client secret.

- Requesting a Realtime client secret with model `gpt-live-1-codex` returns 404 `model_not_found`.
- A separate public Realtime WebRTC test with a fresh secret for `gpt-realtime-2.1` fails with a server error during the requested response. A completed voice response was not verified.

## Related reports

- #51367 describes custom-provider credentials being retained when the Live call URL is overridden. This looks related to the routing mechanism, but its custom gateway key differs from this documented OpenAI-issued SIWC token.
- #40140's explicit model workaround is already applied.
- #15237 proposed SIWC realtime client-secret authentication, but is closed and unmerged; it may also refer to a different ChatGPT authentication flow.

## Expected outcome

Please clarify whether the new OSS SIWC grant supports Codex Live v3 today. If supported, a working provider/authentication configuration or required exchange would help. If unsupported, explicit documentation and an actionable app-server error would let third-party apps avoid asking users to complete a login that cannot enable voice.

I can provide sanitized request IDs through an appropriate support channel if needed.

items.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using?

ChatGPT-hosted Codex task on 2026-10-10. The exact desktop/app build number is not exposed in this environment.

For implementation comparison, I inspected public `openai/codex` commit `cc7ba33601286a751477832b01de7b6f8de0dd9c`.

### What subscription do you have?

Not collected for this report.

### What platform is your computer?

Managed Linux cloud task using the host-owned `codex_apps` MCP server and cloud/user Skills.

### What issue are you seeing?

Cloud Skill package roots can be listed and read, and their root response advertises exact child-resource URIs in `_meta.resources`. Reading any advertised child URI then fails.

Observed behavior:

- Top-level `resources/list` contains the `mcp/skill` package root.
- Reading the package root succeeds.
- The root response includes entries such as:
  `skill://user/<skill-id>/<skill-name>/references/example.md`
- Direct MCP `resources/read` for that advertised URI returns:
  `-32002: Unknown resource`
- `skills.read` with the same package and exact child URI returns:
  `failed to read skill resource`

This reproduced with reference files from two different user Skill packages, so it is not isolated to one package or one missing file.

The package root may also expose a bundle URL, but that is not an equivalent documented child-resource read path and should not be required for `skills.read`.

### Steps to reproduce

1. In a hosted task with a user/cloud Skill that contains a reference file, list the available Skills.
2. Read the Skill package root. Confirm that this succeeds.
3. Inspect the root resource response and copy one exact child URI from `_meta.resources`.
4. Call `skills.read` with the original package and that full child URI.
5. Alternatively, call MCP `resources/read` against `codex_apps` with the same URI.
6. Observe `failed to read skill resource` from `skills.read` and `Unknown resource` from MCP.

### Expected behavior

Every child URI advertised by a Skill package root should be readable through the same `codex_apps` authority using `resources/read`, and therefore through `skills.read`.

At minimum, the server should not advertise a child URI that its resolver cannot return.

### Additional information

The public Codex client appears to preserve the requested URI correctly:

- `codex-rs/ext/skills/src/tools/read.rs` keeps the supplied complete resource URI in `SkillReadRequest.resource`. Provider errors are intentionally flattened to the model-visible `failed to read skill resource`.
- `codex-rs/codex-mcp/src/resource_client.rs` forwards that URI directly in `ReadResourceRequestParams`.

That makes the observed repair boundary the cloud Skill provider / `codex_apps` child-resource registration or resolver, rather than URI rewriting in the public client.

Impact: Skills whose `SKILL.md` requires reading bundled references or scripts cannot follow their own instructions through the documented `skills.read` path.

items.title: [Linux/Niri/Wayland] Floating voice helper blocks clicks and respawns; closing it ends voice
items.body:
## Summary

On native Wayland under Niri, ChatGPT's floating voice helper creates a large transparent surface that intercepts clicks outside the visible controls. Closing the helper ends voice, and hiding/moving it once is insufficient because the app recreates it. This report adds a reproduced **Niri** case and a verified desktop workaround to the related Hyprland reports.

## Environment

- CachyOS / Arch Linux, Niri `26.04 (8ed0da4)`.
- ChatGPT Linux preview, installed package `chatgpt-bin 26.1007.21434-1` (pacman metadata; About-dialog version not independently collected).
- Native Wayland launch with `--ozone-platform=wayland`; separate main and floating helper windows are reported by Niri.
- Main output: 2752 × 1152 logical pixels, 3440 × 1440 physical pixels, scale 1.25.
- Helper: approximately 1132 × 2273 logical pixels, far larger than its visible voice controls.

## Reproduction

1. Start a voice call in ChatGPT on native Wayland under Niri.
2. Focus another application; the floating voice helper appears.
3. Click the underlying application away from the visible voice controls. The transparent helper surface blocks clicks.
4. Remove compositor blur/decorations: the giant visible panel disappears, but clicks are still blocked.
5. Hide the mini helper or move it manually to another workspace. It can be recreated on the current workspace after subsequent focus changes.
6. Close the helper: voice ends as well.

## Expected behavior

Only actual interactive controls should accept pointer input. The rest of the helper should remain transparent and allow clicks through, including after recreation. A persistent option to hide the floating helper while retaining voice in the main app would also address the usability problem.

## Observations and failed attempts

- Blur, shadow, border, and related effects made the oversized transparent canvas visually obvious. Disabling those effects solved only the visual panel, not input interception.
- Compact sizing rules did not shrink the live helper. A direct Niri IPC request for 320 × 160 left it at 1132 × 2273.
- “Hide mini” did not remain effective during voice; the app recreated the helper.
- Moving it fully off-screen was clamped by Niri, leaving a visible corner.
- The large animation canvas may be intentional. This report does **not** establish whether the app sends an incorrect input region, fails to reapply it after recreation, or whether Niri mishandles it. A minimal input-region reproduction/compositor comparison would help isolate responsibility.

## Verified workaround and screenshots

My workaround repository: **https://github.com/natersalad/niri-chatgpt-workaround**

Detailed investigation, four screenshots, installation/removal instructions, and remaining upstream work: https://github.com/natersalad/niri-chatgpt-workaround/blob/main/docs/diagnosis.md

The Python watcher uses Niri IPC to move only the matching oversized helper to an inactive named workspace, without following focus or closing it. It automatically handles new helper IDs and helpers that return to the main workspace. Optional saved coordinates position newly parked helpers on that hidden workspace. The app stays on native Wayland and keeps its normal updates; no app patch is installed.

Live checks verified parking across several recreated helpers, re-parking an existing helper, and saved positioning. I confirmed that moving the helper away preserves voice and unblocks clicks, and that the resulting placement worked well. There are 20 automated tests for the selection and guarded actions. Fresh-login startup has not yet been tested.

This remains a workaround: the helper still exists, can briefly appear before being moved, and its floating controls are unavailable on the main workspace. Code/docs were generated with Codex and checked locally. Screenshots are real desktop captures, already published with permission.

Before, with compositor effects exposing the canvas:

![Oversized helper over the desktop](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/natersalad/niri-chatgpt-workaround/25903492544123c025cb2f070bc255c0b18be3ba/docs/screenshots/before-overlay.png)

After parking, with the helper alive on another workspace:

![Main desktop after parking the helper](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/natersalad/niri-chatgpt-workaround/25903492544123c025cb2f070bc255c0b18be3ba/docs/screenshots/after-parking.png)

## Related reports

- #50963 — similar voice-widget click blocking on Hyprland; closed as not planned.
- #48018 — oversized overlay on Hyprland; closed as duplicate, with a compositor-specific explanation.
- https://github.com/hyprwm/Hyprland/discussions/11834 — input-region discussion for Hyprland. That compositor's patch cannot be applied to Niri.

Please investigate the native Wayland helper's input behavior on Niri, including recreation during voice, and consider a hide-helper-without-ending-voice option. This report was prepared with Codex at my explicit request.

The official X Ads MCP cannot complete native Codex OAuth. It fails before an authorization URL is emitted:

```text
OAuth authorization endpoint origin does not match the authorization server origin without issuer-bound callbacks
```

The dedicated X app is configured as a Native App / Public client, with Read and write permissions and Ads Project access. No client secret is supplied.

Configure a pre-registered public client:

```toml
[mcp_servers.x_ads]

```

Run:

```sh
codex mcp login x_ads --no-browser --scopes ads.read,ads.write,offline.access
```

Normal browser login also fails at the same validation. A server-specific callback URL did not change the outcome; the error happens before callback registration can be verified.

## Public discovery metadata

The protected resource at https://ads-api.x.com/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource declares `https://api.x.com` as its authorization server.

`authorization_response_iss_parameter_supported` is absent. These public endpoints were read without credentials.

## Expected behavior

Please provide a supported connection path for this official provider that preserves issuer binding, state, S256 PKCE, refresh-token protection, and exact callback matching; or coordinate RFC 9207 authorization-response support with X. I am not requesting a global validation bypass.

```text
2026-10-10T22:30:57.858Z primary_runtime_validation_finished bundleVersion=26.1009.11318 outcome=passed problemCount=0
2026-10-10T22:31:37.056Z sa_server_request_failed errorMessage="Workspace routing is unavailable" routePattern=/wham/onboarding/context status=432
```

Failures recur over several minutes. The application window exists, renderer is marked visible, and app-server config/read and thread/attachment/list requests also succeed; this does not look like a missing CLI or failed MSIX registration.

items.title: Computer Use on Windows cannot control elevated (administrator) apps — e.g. games like Genshin Impact

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: windows-os
labels.description: Issues related to Codex on Windows systems

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

items.body:
### What happens

Windows Computer Use cannot interact with elevated (administrator) apps: input never reaches the target window.

Concrete case: **Genshin Impact (原神)**. Its client (`YuanShen.exe` / `GenshinImpact.exe`) declares `requireAdministrator` in its manifest — the launcher and anti-cheat are elevated too, so the game always runs at High integrity. Asking Computer Use to click/type in the running game window does nothing; the input is silently dropped.

### Why

Windows UIPI (User Interface Privilege Isolation): a medium-integrity process cannot inject input (SendInput / PostMessage / SetForegroundWindow / UI Automation) into a high-integrity (elevated) window. The Computer Use injector inherits the desktop app's integrity (medium), so it is blocked by design.

### Why it cannot be worked around locally

- The Codex/ChatGPT desktop app on Windows is an MSIX/Store package (`OpenAI.Codex`), so it cannot be launched elevated.
- `codex features list` (desktop 26.1007.2314.0) shows `elevated_windows_sandbox = removed` and `windows_sandbox_service = under development (false)` — there is no supported switch.
- Disabling UAC (`EnableLUA=0`) or using the built-in Administrator gives a single unfiltered token, which breaks MSIX/AppContainer activation entirely (Store apps then fail with "This app can't open"), so it is not viable.
- Running `codex exec` elevated still reports "Computer Use native connection is unavailable" (the native pipe is hosted by the desktop app), so the CLI cannot substitute.

### Expected

A supported way for Computer Use to drive elevated apps on Windows, e.g. a UIAccess-signed (`uiAccess=true`) input helper in a protected location, input routed through a privileged service, or an opt-in elevated-input mode.

### Impact

Blocks automation of every admin-level desktop app — most Windows games (Genshin Impact, Honkai: Star Rail, ...), plus installers and admin tools.

Configuring one regular file as a writable root prevents the Linux sandbox from starting the command. Instead, setup attempts child paths such as `README.md/.git` and `README.md/.aws` and fails with ENOTDIR.

Observed on the installed Linux x64 Codex CLI 0.162.1. Executable SHA-256: `628e35487d888a28f0427fc37501da529dd3d81fcbad7a2c3421c1e8670d92e1`. A run with six synthetic readable inputs, one exact writable README, and networking disabled exited 101 before its Python probe. No fixture changed. The paths and child PID below are normalized; this is not evidence of successful access-denial tests.

```text
bwrap: Can't mkdir parents for /tmp/codex-file-root-repro/worker/README.md/.git: Not a directory

thread 'main' (<child-pid>) panicked at linux-sandbox/src/linux_run_main.rs:1275:21:
failed to inspect synthetic bubblewrap mount target /tmp/codex-file-root-repro/worker/README.md/.aws: Not a directory (os error 20)
note: run with `RUST_BACKTRACE=1` environment variable to display a backtrace
```

The public source at tag `rust-v0.162.1`, commit `092d3acd6bec3e3a14bdc7e7a2810ab628ab759d`, applies metadata masking to each writable root and computes `root.join(name)` without a directory check in that function: [call site](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/092d3acd6bec3e3a14bdc7e7a2810ab628ab759d/codex-rs/linux-sandbox/src/bwrap.rs#L700), [masking function](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/092d3acd6bec3e3a14bdc7e7a2810ab628ab759d/codex-rs/linux-sandbox/src/bwrap.rs#L842). This matches the observed child paths. It is not a claim of a bit-for-bit rebuild from that tag.

Proposed smaller reproduction, NOT RUN in this two-file form:

Use a fresh absolute `@REPRO_ROOT@` with `worker/`, empty `home/`, `codex-home/` and `tmp/`. Put these invented texts in the two worker files:

`worker/README.md`:
```text
# Example

This synthetic README is the only writable application file.

```

`worker/source.txt`:
```text
Synthetic source: this file must remain read-only.

```

Write the following synthetic configuration to `codex-home/config.toml`, substituting `@REPRO_ROOT@` and `@CODEX_BINARY@` with absolute paths. The binary path is an existing official Linux executable.

```toml
approval_policy = "never"
default_permissions = "file-root-repro"
project_doc_max_bytes = 0
permissions = { "file-root-repro" = { filesystem = { ":minimal" = "read", "@CODEX_BINARY@" = "read", "@REPRO_ROOT@/worker/README.md" = "write", "@REPRO_ROOT@/worker/source.txt" = "read" }, network = { enabled = false } } }
mcp_servers = {}
```

Proposed invocation and environment; bound the process to 15 seconds. This is a preparation recipe, not a claim that the simplified invocation has been executed:

```json
{
  "argv": [
    "@CODEX_BINARY@",
    "sandbox",
    "--permission-profile",
    "file-root-repro",
    "--cd",
    "@REPRO_ROOT@/worker",
    "--",
    "/usr/bin/python3",
    "-B",
    "-c",
    "from pathlib import Path; p=Path('source.txt'); assert p.read_text()=='Synthetic source: this file must remain read-only.\\n'; Path('README.md').write_text('# Example\\n\\nEdited synthetic README.\\n'); print('PROBE_COMPLETED')"
  ],
  "env": {
    "PATH": "/usr/bin:/bin",
    "HOME": "@REPRO_ROOT@/home",
    "CODEX_HOME": "@REPRO_ROOT@/codex-home",
    "TMPDIR": "@REPRO_ROOT@/tmp",
    "LANG": "C.UTF-8",
    "PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE": "1"
  },
  "timeout_seconds": 15,
  "status": "NOT_RUN"
}
```

Expected: the command runs, reads the exact source file, updates README only and prints `PROBE_COMPLETED`. Observed in the larger synthetic run: setup fails before the command while treating a regular writable file as a directory. Other prerequisites, including daemon/socket configuration, should be diagnosed separately.

No model, login, MCP server or upstream generation is needed for this sandbox-only case. No writable-directory substitution or sandbox bypass is proposed. The smaller fixture and probe are explicitly untested; maintainers should reproduce and qualify any correction independently.

items.title: macOS alpha.17.2: hundreds of per-chat MCP helpers and synchronized startup/refresh bursts

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: mcp

labels.name: app

items.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using?

ChatGPT desktop 26.1007.21159, build 20052, with bundled `codex-cli 0.162.0-alpha.17.2`.

### What subscription do you have?

Not collected for this incident.

### What platform is your computer?

macOS 27.0, build 26A5388g, Apple Silicon, 12 logical CPUs, 48 GB RAM. `uname -mprs`: `Darwin 27.0.0 arm64 arm`.

### What issue are you seeing?

A long-lived desktop app-server accumulated hundreds of MCP/helper processes, and stopping them provided only temporary relief: the same app-server recreated large per-chat helper sets. Its logs also show synchronized MCP startup failures and readiness traffic across 28 loaded chats. The Mac became difficult to use under severe CPU and scheduler pressure.

This is a current-version report of **per-loaded-chat resource amplification and startup/refresh bursts**, not a claim that every helper is orphaned or that repeated `ready` notifications prove a process launch.

Incident measurements on October 10, 2026 (UTC):

| Observation | Measured result |
| --- | --- |
| Initial app-server age | Approximately 21 hours |
| Initial process tree | 470 processes including the app-server; 290 direct children |
| Selected initial descendants | 90 bundled computer-use Node processes, 81 native `SkyComputerUseClient` processes, 61 `node_repl` processes, and 95 npm wrappers for Context7, codemode and XcodeBuildMCP, plus other descendants |
| Targeted cleanup | 278 direct MCP/computer-use helpers plus 137 nested helpers (415 total) terminated cleanly with SIGTERM; no SIGKILL required |
| Immediate result | App-server direct children fell to two; three subsequent samples showed zero selected MCP/computer-use helpers |
| Recurrence | Direct children later returned to 243, then settled around 224 in another sample |
| Follow-up native-client breakdown | 28 `event-stream mcp`, 28 `computer-history mcp`, 28 `messages mcp` |
| Other follow-up direct children | 28 `node_repl`, 28 `node cua-repl.mjs`, 56 other bundled Node processes, and 25 Context7 npm wrappers |

The three native-client groups are **different integrations**, not evidence of three leaked generations. Parentage was verified; these were still children of the desktop app-server, not PID-1 orphans.

Desktop logs recorded:

- 21:11 UTC: 959 MCP startup-status events across 28 distinct chat IDs, including 485 `starting` and 202 `failed` events.
- 21:12 UTC: at least 1,090 such events across 28 chats in the snapshot, including at least 185 failures.
- Repeated Context7, codemode and XcodeBuildMCP handshake timeouts, including many failures in the same second.
- Host and thread `mcpServerStatus/list` calls taking approximately 32 seconds, with requests coming from both a visible and a hidden renderer window.

Sanitized backend examples:

```text
codex_mcp::rmcp_client
mcp.runtime.refresh_if_dirty:mcp.runtime.refresh:new{server_name=xcodebuildmcp}:
MCP server startup failed ... timed out handshaking with MCP server after 30s

codex_mcp::rmcp_client
mcp.runtime.refresh_if_dirty:mcp.runtime.refresh:new{server_name=codemode}:
MCP server startup failed ... timed out handshaking with MCP server after 30s
```

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Observed workflow; a clean-install minimal reproducer has not yet been isolated:

1. Use the desktop app over a long session with multiple loaded chats and several local stdio MCP integrations, including bundled computer-use integrations.
2. Leave completed/idle chats loaded alongside active chats.
3. Observe process count and parentage during MCP refresh/startup activity.
4. Compare process creation with status notifications, startup failures and concurrent host/thread status requests.

Emergency cleanup was performed after observation, so the recurrence after killing helpers is an **intervention result**, not an independent proof of the original trigger. Closed clients are expected to reconnect; the problematic behavior to investigate is the aggregate eager work and resource retention across loaded chats, including the concurrent startup burst.

### What is the expected behavior?

Loaded idle chats should not impose hundreds of resident helpers or a large simultaneous startup wave. Please investigate lazy startup for ordinary chats, bounded host-wide startup concurrency and retries, idle runtime unloading, and deduplication of unchanged status notifications. Stateful MCP servers may require per-chat isolation; indiscriminate sharing is not the proposed fix.

### Additional information: source trace and limits of attribution

Inspection of the exact installed release tag, `rust-v0.162.0-alpha.17.2`, establishes relevant mechanisms:

- [`build_mcp_runtime_input`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.162.0-alpha.17.2/codex-rs/core/src/session/mcp_runtime.rs) selects `LazyWhenCached` for subagents and `Eager` for ordinary sessions.
- [`invalidate_mcp_runtimes`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.162.0-alpha.17.2/codex-rs/core/src/thread_manager.rs) requests refresh for every loaded thread.
- [`start_mcp_prewarm_worker`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.162.0-alpha.17.2/codex-rs/core/src/session/mcp_prewarm.rs) responds to per-session refresh requests and authentication changes.
- [`McpRuntime::replace`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.162.0-alpha.17.2/codex-rs/codex-mcp/src/runtime.rs) and the [connection manager](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.162.0-alpha.17.2/codex-rs/codex-mcp/src/connection_manager.rs) do contain connection-reuse logic. This report does not claim cleanup/reuse is entirely absent.

The exact event initiating the original refresh burst remains unisolated. The source trace supports the observed fan-out, but is not proof of an infinite feedback loop or a specific broken ownership edge.

The owner reported a 1-minute load average of 199 and an earlier peak of 328. During investigation, `top` samples showed approximately 96–99% CPU busy. **Other workloads were substantial:** concurrent test jobs, a development VM, desktop rendering, monitoring, and initially Time Machine. A brief controlled suspension of the affected app-server and 280 helper processes still left roughly 83–85% CPU busy in subsequent interval samples. All suspended processes were resumed. Therefore this report does not attribute all host CPU usage or the reported peak exclusively to Codex.

Local mitigation so far: targeted helper cleanup, lower scheduling priority for background development/monitoring workloads, and cancellation of the current Time Machine backup. A desktop/app-server restart can clear loaded runtime state, but is a workaround rather than a verified upstream fix.

Related: #50627 (readiness/inventory traffic), #50637 (native helper retention), #30408 (per-thread MCP process growth), #38754 (repeated stdio startup). This report adds the current alpha version, high process counts, measured post-cleanup recurrence, invocation-mode breakdown, and a controlled CPU-attribution check.

Only sanitized aggregates, public source links and abbreviated error text are included. No raw logs, chat contents, credentials, local account paths or private project source are attached.

2. The documented call `await sky.launch_app({app:'C:\\Windows\\explorer.exe'});` initially returned the targetable-window error above, both before and after a full PC reboot. The owner observed Edge appearing after these requests despite no Edge launch being requested. The internal app-resolution path and causality are unproven.
3. The owner opened Explorer manually. `list_windows()` returned a uniquely selected window with `app: process:C:\Windows\explorer.exe` and title `Home - File Explorer`. `get_window()` used that returned ID and app; no handles were guessed.
4. An address-bar focus attempt using Control_L+l, followed by text-only get_window_state, returned accessibility:null. No path or other text was typed because focus could not be verified. The owner reported an Explorer hang and abnormal input behavior, recovering after Escape and the Computer Use UI closing.
5. After the owner changed an unspecified setting and authorized a bounded retry, launch_app succeeded and exposed a targetable Explorer window. The exact setting was not recorded, so no causal claim is made.
6. With explicit permission to capture that Explorer Home window, get_window_state identified Explorer but returned images of Chrome and Codex/desktop regions. Accessibility and focused-element information remained null. Those screenshots are omitted because they contain unrelated private content.
7. One fresh enumeration, unique Explorer selection, and activate_window recovery attempt returned the timeout above. The owner reported Explorer hanging again. Native inputs were stopped; no further reproduction was attempted.

Minimal relevant API path:

```javascript
const {sky} = await import('@oai/sky');
const matches = (await sky.list_windows()).filter(
  w => String(w.app).toLowerCase() === 'process:c:\\windows\\explorer.exe'
);
if (matches.length !== 1) throw new Error('Non-unique Explorer selection');
const window = await sky.get_window({id:matches[0].id,app:matches[0].app});
const state = await sky.get_window_state({
  window, include_screenshot:true, include_text:true
});
// Observed: Explorer identity, wrong desktop images, accessibility:null.
// A subsequent fresh selection and activate_window() timed out.
```

This summarizes calls already performed, not an additional reproduction.

### What is the expected behavior?

Capture and control the explicitly selected Explorer window consistently, or fail clearly before input is sent. Do not present another window's pixels as the selected-window observation. An explicit Explorer launch should not unexpectedly open another application. Native observation and activation should not leave Explorer unresponsive.

Please investigate window identity/capture routing, Explorer accessibility/activation, and the earlier executable-to-app resolution error. Shared versus separate root causes remain unknown.

### Additional information

## Environment and read-only checks

- Desktop app 26.1007.21434, build 13901, prod channel; updater reported up_to_date during investigation.
- Windows package 26.1007.2314.0; bundled Computer Use plugin 26.1007.21434; @oai/sky 0.7.6, native helper codex-computer-use-swift.exe.
- Explorer fixed numeric version 10.0.26100.9444 matches the hang events. Descriptive version 10.0.26100.8117 is a distinct field, not by itself proof of mismatched files.
- RTX 4070, Windows driver 32.0.16.1088; Intel Core i9-13900KF; approximately 32 GB RAM.
- Explorer/helper Authenticode signatures were valid Microsoft/OpenAI signatures. Four inspected helper/runtime files matched packaged copies.
- CPU was approximately 2-13%, about 18.4 GB RAM available, both disks Healthy/OK with ample free space.
- No WHEA, disk, NTFS, storage-controller, Display/nvlddmkm, or resource-exhaustion events in the checked seven-day System log. Older graphics live-dump reports and a boot-time CPU performance-limiting warning exist but are not proven related; queued reports must not be mistaken for new failures at their later logging time.
- Protected WER report files were inaccessible; no process dump or stack was inspected. These checks do not exclude every hardware/driver fault.
- Some earlier captures were blocked by approval review because Explorer Home can show private filenames. The later capture was explicitly authorized and did execute. Wrong-window capture and activation timeout are distinct from those approval rejections.

## Separate settings observation; not established as the hang cause

Settings showed Any App and Chrome enabled, with Explorer/Python always-allowed, yet Configuration warned that computer_use.windows.always_allowed_app_ids was ignored. The current TOML parses and contains a boolean map under [computer_use.windows.always_allowed_app_ids].

Read-only inspection of installed app.asar/.vite/build/main-BklS_2Y2.js (SHA-256 5cf1544463be9497b85b69051aa5ad32320f9ebdca063ec2ab41abb75b6cadf7) confirmed desktop writer ehe builds this table via Object.fromEntries(e.map(e=>[e,!0])); reader Uw selects true Object.entries after schema validation; Windows path selection Xw targets the main config.toml. Public configuration docs describe an array of strings, which is not a safe replacement for this installed desktop reader/writer.

A screenshot also warns about features.guardianv2.thread_context, but the current user config has no thread_context, guardian feature entry, or profile overrides. The source/freshness of that warning is unproven. Settings were preserved unchanged.

## Related reports and scope

- #43072 reports earlier Explorer screenshots showing Codex and launch/UIA failures. This report adds current-build activation timeouts, null accessibility data, and two Windows-confirmed Explorer AppHangB1 events. No shared root cause is claimed.
- #47427 already tracks the separate approval-table warning; included here as troubleshooting context, not as a claimed cause of the hangs.

No private project files, raw chat transcripts, screenshots, credentials, browser data, or memory dumps are included. No application source, installer, browser profile, or system setting was changed in the read-only diagnosis.

26.1007.21159 (build 20052), verified from the installed application's Info.plist. Bundle identifier: `com.openai.codex`. The About dialog was not used for this measurement.

### What subscription do you have?

Not recorded in this diagnostic report.

### What platform is your computer?

macOS 27.0.1 (26A434), Apple silicon / ARM64, 64 GiB system memory.

### What issue are you seeing?

The Codex main window repeatedly stops accepting mouse and keyboard input while other applications remain usable. The native macOS menu bar still works. Normal quitting is possible; force quit was not required.

This has occurred at least twice, with the latest occurrence investigated on October 10, 2026, around 15:00–15:10 America/Chicago. Quitting and relaunching restored access temporarily, but the problem returned and is repeatedly interrupting work.

An earlier diagnostic exchange incorrectly characterized the menu bar as unresponsive. The user's explicit correction is authoritative: **the menu bar remained usable**.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Observed sequence, not a deterministic minimal reproduction:

1. Use the Codex desktop app normally.
2. The main window begins ignoring mouse clicks and keyboard input.
3. Check other applications: their mouse and keyboard input still work.
4. Use the macOS menu bar: it remains usable, including the ability to quit normally.
5. Quit and relaunch Codex. Input returns temporarily, but the failure occurs again.

The exact triggering action and recurrence interval are unknown. Whether Computer Use was involved immediately before either occurrence is also unknown. No attachment, chat-reference, or specific project trigger has been established.

### What is the expected behavior?

The main window should continue accepting input during normal operation. Recovery should not require repeated application restarts. If a particular task or UI surface is blocked, the rest of the window should remain usable.

### Additional information

**App remains alive during the input failure**

Read-only tools and background communication continued during diagnosis. Three-second macOS `sample` captures were collected for the main application process and two renderer processes.

- The main application's main thread spent 262 of 265 sampled observations in its run-loop event wait, with occasional timer/source handling.
- The two sampled renderer main threads were predominantly in event waits (275/275 and 262/265 observations on those paths).
- These short samples do not identify the cause. They do not demonstrate a sustained main-thread busy loop and do not rule out input-routing or other UI-state failures. Symbols in the packaged Chromium/Electron framework are incomplete, so distant symbol names were not treated as precise source locations.

**High-load confounder tested**

Three `codebase-memory-mcp` helper processes were found using approximately one CPU core each and roughly 25 GiB combined resident memory. Only those three helpers were temporarily suspended. They subsequently showed 0% CPU, and the one-minute system load average fell from about 59 to 32. **The user explicitly confirmed that input still did not work after that intervention.** The high load is not established as the cause of the window-input failure.

**Update offer discrepancy**

The in-chat desktop update-check tool reported installed version 26.1007.21159 / build 20052 and an available version 26.1007.30912 / build 20156. However, the user reports that the application is not offering an upgrade, so they have not installed one. Please do not interpret this report as the user declining an actionable update. It is unknown whether the other build fixes this problem.

**Possibly related reports**

- #52242 describes loss of mouse and keyboard input with native menus still working, associated with image paste/drag operations.
- #34555 describes an unresponsive desktop window while backend work continues, associated with large chat references.

Those triggers have not been confirmed here, and a common root cause has not been established.

## Description

The separate **Plan Mode document panel** in the Codex desktop app does not properly display Hebrew (right-to-left) content. When a plan is written in Hebrew and opened in the dedicated plan document viewer, **everything is aligned to the left**, even paragraphs containing only Hebrew and no English text.

This is distinct from the main chat: RTL formatting in the regular conversation is imperfect but still reasonably readable, whereas the separate plan document panel is substantially harder to read.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open the Codex desktop app on Windows.
2. Start a conversation in Hebrew in Plan Mode.
3. Ask Codex to produce a detailed plan in Hebrew.
4. Open the generated plan in its separate document panel.
5. Observe that even Hebrew-only paragraphs, headings, and lists are left-aligned.

## Expected behavior

Hebrew-only text in the plan document should flow right-to-left and be right-aligned, including headings, paragraphs, and lists. Mixed-direction content should handle Hebrew and English correctly, while code blocks can remain left-to-right.

## Actual behavior

The entire plan document is left-aligned, even without any English mixed in. This significantly reduces readability and usability for long plans.

## Additional context

- The issue affects the **separate plan document panel**, not merely the Plan Mode response displayed in the chat.
- It is especially noticeable when comparing the same Hebrew content in the regular chat against the document panel.
- Related general RTL issues: #32157, #30129, #19504.

items.title: App-server: admission deadlines and recoverable delivery IDs for externally submitted input

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: app-server
labels.description: Issues involving app server protocol or interfaces

items.body:
## Summary

Please consider optional runtime-enforced admission deadlines and recoverable delivery identities for external app-server input. These would let durable external controllers recover from lost responses without duplicating input, and distinguish cancellation before admission from cancellation that arrived too late.

This complements **#38289 (atomic idle-only turn admission)** rather than requesting a second version of that API. The request here concerns delivery identity, expiry, and recovery around admission. The capabilities could be delivered incrementally.

## Use case and present workaround

An external scheduler waits until work is due, targets an existing exact thread, and either requests idle delivery or steers an identified active turn. It persists its own submission journal before calling Codex.

For compatibility with unmodified Codex, that controller can enforce deadlines and cancellation only at its own dispatch boundary. Once a request may have reached Codex, a client timeout does not prove rejection; queued input may be consumed later. A client-side journal alone cannot make runtime input admission transactional with that journal.

The intended workaround is conservative: preserve uncertain outcomes, reconcile available evidence, and do not automatically resubmit ambiguous input. This request seeks supported primitives to improve that contract, not a new scheduling engine inside Codex.

## Requested semantics

Field and operation names below are illustrative, not assertions about existing APIs.

1. **A caller-provided logical delivery identity**, scoped to an authorized runtime/thread and bound to the canonical input and admission options. Concurrent or repeated submissions of the same identity and payload should resolve to the same admission decision, not append the input again. Reusing an identity with conflicting content should produce a typed conflict.

2. **A durable receipt lookup** for that identity. It should distinguish pending/staged, admitted (with the actual input/turn correlation), cancelled, expired, rejected, and unknown/receipt-unavailable as applicable. A transport acknowledgment should not be mistaken for proof that input was admitted. Please document restart, retention, and runtime-generation behavior; an unavailable or expired receipt must not silently become proof of non-admission.

3. **An optional latest-admission deadline**, checked by the runtime at the boundary that actually admits the input. For retained queue input, checking only at enqueue time would not prevent consumption after expiry while the external controller is disconnected. This is an admission deadline, not a deadline for model or tool execution to finish.

4. **A cancellation result ordered against admission.** If cancellation wins, delayed submissions carrying that delivery identity must not later admit input. If admission wins, cancellation should report already admitted with the available receipt, not claim to undo it. Cancelling a delivery should not implicitly interrupt an unrelated active turn.

Idle-only preconditions should compose with the operation requested in #38289 at the authoritative thread-input boundary. Where these capabilities apply to steering, preserve the existing explicit active-turn match rather than retargeting another turn.

## Useful qualification scenarios

- Two concurrent same-ID/same-payload requests admit one input; a conflicting payload is rejected.
- Lose the response after admission, reconnect (including after a server restart), and recover the original outcome without appending input again.
- Leave input queued while the client is offline past its deadline; it is not consumed after that deadline.
- Race cancellation with a delayed submission; distinguish cancellation-won from admission-won, and preserve that result across restart within the documented retention contract.
- Race an idle-only request with human input; reject without steering when the idle precondition no longer holds.

## Scope and evidence limits

This is a feature request, not a claim of a newly reproduced regression in a particular release. If an existing supported interface already supplies some of these guarantees, documentation of its precise semantics and version requirements would be useful.

No changes to approval/sandbox policy, authentication bypass, arbitrary access to other threads, built-in Temporal integration, or exactly-once downstream shell/tool effects are requested. Input admission and completion of the work caused by that input are separate concerns.

Reference: https://developers.openai.com/codex/app-server
Related: https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/38289

Reuse and prewarm the WSL clipboard text reader

## Why

WSL clipboard reads previously launched PowerShell for every paste. Process creation can hang under WSL and stall the shared clipboard worker.

## What changed

- Reuse a persistent PowerShell reader on a dedicated thread, keeping clipboard requests bounded by their deadlines and restarting the reader after errors.
- Prewarm the reader at startup when right-click paste is allowed on WSL, without accessing clipboard contents.
- Use length-framed UTF-8 responses to preserve whitespace and distinguish consecutive pastes while enforcing message size limits.

## Testing

Update the command-reader test to cover consecutive responses from one process, large clipboard text, UTF-8 and whitespace preservation, and read timeouts.
